title: Totals that stay right when the stream turns parallel

blocks.text: A parallel `reduce` splits the stream into chunks, reduces each chunk from the identity, and combines the partial results. That is only correct when the operation is **associative**, when the identity really is an identity (`identity op x == x`), and, for the three-argument `reduce(identity, accumulator, combiner)`, when the combiner merges two partial results the way the accumulator would have.
Write three static methods in `Totals`. Each receives a stream that may be sequential or parallel, and must give the same answer either way:

items: `int balance(Stream<Integer> withdrawals, int opening)`: the opening balance minus every withdrawal.
`int withBonus(Stream<Integer> scores, int bonus)`: the sum of the scores plus the bonus, counted once.
`int totalLength(Stream<String> words)`: the total number of characters, with the three-argument `reduce`.

blocks.text: A version that only passes sequential streams is not done: the tests also hand it large parallel streams.

cases.says: It computes the balance, the bonus total and the total length of a sequential stream.
The balance is the same on a parallel stream: subtraction is not associative, so it cannot be the reducer.
The bonus is added once on a parallel stream: a bonus used as the identity is added once per chunk.
The total length is the same on a parallel stream: the combiner must add the partial totals of the chunks.

concepts: A parallel reduce is correct only with an associative operation; subtraction is not one.
The combiner of a three-argument reduce merges the partial results of two chunks and must agree with the accumulator.
A parallel stream splits its source, processes the chunks on several threads and combines the partial results.
The identity of a parallel reduce is applied once per chunk, so it must leave every element unchanged.
